name: HAWKE, the Hon. Alexander (Alex) George

headline.note: The only identified private-sector role was part-time retail work in 1998, with hours and exact dates unavailable. Army Reserve service lacks paid-duty and FTE evidence. Political staff, party activity, study and elected office are excluded under the codebook; missing evidence is not zero.

career_spells.role: Bachelor of Arts (Government and Philosophy) and Master of Public Affairs and Government student
career_spells.evidence_note: The current official biography identifies both University of Sydney qualifications; the secondary biography says Army Reserve and retail work occurred while he was at university. Enrolment, completion dates, study load and work overlaps are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Study is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.employer: Australian Army Reserve — Royal Australian Armoured Corps, 1st/15th Royal New South Wales Lancers
career_spells.evidence_note: The official biography records Army Reserve service from 1995 to 2000 and identifies the corps, unit and rank. Training, paid-duty days, hours, breaks and overlap with study and retail work are unresolved; Reserve service is not assumed to be full-time.
career_spells.counting_note: Public military service is supported, but no substantive full-time interval or FTE is established.

career_spells.evidence_note: The frozen official record says retail manager in 1998. The secondary biography, citing a contemporary Sydney Morning Herald profile, identifies Woolworths in the Hills District, assistant-manager duties and part-time work while studying. Exact dates, hours, FTE and leave are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: The role was part-time and lacks an FTE fraction, so no full-time-equivalent total is calculated.

career_spells.employer: Office of Ross Cameron MP, Member for Parramatta
career_spells.evidence_note: The secondary biography records this as Hawke's first post-graduation political staff role, before his 2001 move to Senator Coonan's office. Start and end dates, employing entity, hours and leave are unresolved, and the frozen occupation extract omits it.
career_spells.counting_note: Political staff employment is excluded from the narrow public/private headline under the codebook.

career_spells.employer: Office of Senator the Hon. Helen Coonan, Minister for Revenue and Assistant Treasurer
career_spells.evidence_note: Official biographies provide year boundaries and identify the minister and portfolio; the secondary biography says his subject areas included taxation, superannuation and insurance. Exact dates, employing department, hours and leave are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Political staff employment is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.employer: Office of the Hon. David Clarke MLC
career_spells.evidence_note: Official biographies identify the adviser role and year boundaries. Exact dates, employing entity, duties, hours and leave are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Political staff employment is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.evidence_note: Official biographies identify an adviser role in 2007 before Hawke's federal election. Exact dates, employing entity, duties, hours, leave and any campaign overlap are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Political staff employment is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.employer: Liberal Party of Australia and Young Liberal Movement
career_spells.role: Member from 1995; NSW Young Liberal vice-president and president; federal Young Liberal president; party office-holder and campaign participant
career_spells.evidence_note: The secondary biography records party membership from 1995, NSW Young Liberal vice-presidency in 2001, presidency from 2002, NSW State Executive service from 2002 to 2005 and federal Young Liberal presidency from 2005. The official biography confirms current Liberal parliamentary service. Remuneration, hours and separation from paid parliamentary-staff roles are unresolved; organisational roles are not assumed to be employment.
career_spells.counting_note: Party activity is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.evidence_note: The frozen roster and current official biography establish House service from the 24 November 2007 election. Ministerial, shadow, committee and party-room offices are nested within elected service.
career_spells.counting_note: Elected office is excluded under the codebook.

sources.title: Frozen official occupation/service extract
sources.note: Frozen record supplies the 1998 retail role, three adviser roles from 2001 to 2007 and House commencement; no roster refresh.

sources.title: Hon Alex Hawke MP

sources.note: Current official biography corroborates qualifications, occupations, Army Reserve service and federal service.

sources.title: Alex Hawke
sources.locator: Early life and Early political career sections with official parliamentary and contemporary press citations
sources.note: Secondary synthesis identifies Woolworths and part-time status, the omitted Ross Cameron electorate role, adviser subject areas and dated party offices.

research_notes: The frozen occupation extract omits Army Reserve service and the Ross Cameron electorate-office role; both are recorded separately with their evidentiary limitations.
Army Reserve service is not treated as full-time employment without paid-duty or FTE evidence.
Overlapping study, Reserve, retail and party activity are preserved rather than forced into a single employment timeline.
Ministerial, parliamentary-party and committee positions after 2007 are nested within elected office, not double-counted as separate employment.
open_questions: What were the exact University of Sydney enrolment and graduation dates and study/work overlaps?
What paid-duty days, hours, breaks and remuneration applied to Army Reserve service from 1995 to 2000?
What were the exact Woolworths dates, weekly hours, FTE and leave in 1998?
What were the exact Ross Cameron electorate-office dates, employing entity, hours and leave?
What were the exact appointment dates, payroll entities, hours and leave for each 2001–2007 adviser role?
Were any Young Liberal or Liberal Party organisational positions separately remunerated?
